31. Programming Is an Act of Design

作者：Einar Landre

Kristen Nygaard, father of object-oriented programming and the Simula programming language, used to say programming is learning . Accepting the fact that programming—or more precisely, software development—is a processes of discovery and learning, not a process of engineering and construction, is fundamental to bringing software practices forward. Applying the concepts of traditional engineering and construction on software development does not work. The problems have been documented and commented upon by leading software thinkers for more than 30 years. As an example, in 1987 Fredric Brooks, Jr., stated in the “Report of the Defense Science Board Task Force on Military Software” that the document-driven, specifythen-build approach lies at the heart of many software problems.

面向对象编程和 Simula 语言之父 Kristen Nygaard 常说：编程就是学习。接受这个事实——编程（或者更准确说软件开发）是一个发现和学习的过程，而不是工程和建造的过程——是把软件实践往前推的根本。把传统工程和建造的概念套在软件开发上行不通。这个问题 30 多年来被顶尖软件思想家记录和评论过。比如 1987 年 Fredric Brooks, Jr. 在《国防科学委员会军事软件任务组报告》中说：文档驱动、先规格后构建的方法是很多软件问题的根源。

So where should the software industry look to improve its practices? What about the industries involved in production of sophisticated mass-market products such as cars, pharmaceutical drugs, or semiconductors?

那软件业该向谁学习改进实践？看看那些生产复杂大众产品的行业——汽车、制药、半导体？

Let’s take a look at the car industry. When planning a new model, the first thing is to choose a concept or archetype. It’s primarily an architectural positioning mechanism. The BMW X6 is an example of a new concept that combines the properties of an SUV and a coupe into what BMW calls a sports activity coupe . Before you can purchase a new X6, BMW has invested thousands of hours and millions of dollars in both its vehicle and manufacturing design. When BMW receives your order, one of its assembly lines will kick in and produce your customized version of the X6.

看看汽车业。规划新车型时，第一件事是选一个概念或原型。这主要是一个架构定位机制。宝马 X6 是一个新概念的例子，把 SUV 和轿跑的属性结合成宝马所谓的运动型多功能轿跑。在你买到新 X6 之前，宝马已经在车辆和制造设计上投入了数千小时和数百万美元。当宝马收到你的订单，它的一条装配线就启动，生产你的定制版 X6。

So what can we learn from this car-maker scenario? The important lesson is that the making of a new car involves two processes: the first process is the creative design process, including establishing the required assembly lines. The second process is the manufacturing of cars in line with customer specifications. In many ways these are the processes we find in the software industry as well. The challenge is what we put into the terms.

那我们能从这个汽车厂场景学到什么？重要教训是：造新车涉及两个过程。第一个过程是创造性设计过程，包括建立所需的装配线。第二个过程是按客户规格制造汽车。在很多方面，这两个过程我们在软件业也能找到。挑战在于我们怎么命名这些过程。

In the article “What is software design?”, Jack Reeves suggests that the only artifact of software engineering that satisfies the criteria for a design document, as such a document is understood and used in classical engineering, is the source code. The manufacturing of the software is automated and taken care of by the compiler, build, and test scripts.

在《什么是软件设计》一文中，Jack Reeves 提出：软件工程里唯一满足「设计文档」标准的制品——按经典工程对这种文档的理解和使用——就是源代码。软件的制造是自动化的，由编译器、构建和测试脚本负责。

By accepting that carving out source code is an act of design, not an act of construction, we are in a position to adopt useful management practices that are proven to work. Those are the practices used to manage creative and unpredictable work such as developing a new car, a new medical drug, or a new computer game. We talk about the practices of agile product management and lean production such as SCRUM. These practices focus on maximizing return on investment in terms of customer value.

接受了「刻源代码是设计行为，不是建造行为」之后，我们就能采用那些被证明有效的管理实践。那些是用来管理创造性、不可预测工作的实践——比如造新车、新药、新电脑游戏。我们说的就是敏捷产品管理和精益生产的实践，比如 Scrum。这些实践聚焦于客户价值意义上的投资回报最大化。

For the software industry to capitalize on these practices, we must remember this: programming is an act of design, not an act of construction.

软件业要从这些实践中受益，必须记住：编程是设计行为，不是建造行为。

32. Give Developers Autonomy

作者：Philip Nelson

Most architects begin their careers as developers. An architect has new responsibilities and greater authority in determining how a system is built. You may find it difficult to let go of what you did as a developer in your new role as an architect. Worse, you may feel it’s important for you to exercise a lot of control over how developers do their work to implement the design. It will be very important to your success and your team’s success to give all of your teammates enough autonomy to exercise their own creativity and abilities.

大多数架构师是从开发做起的。架构师有新的职责，在决定系统怎么建方面有更大权力。你可能发现很难在新架构师角色里放下做开发时做的事。更糟的是，你可能觉得重要的是要对开发怎么实现设计施加大量控制。给所有队友足够的自主权去发挥他们自己的创造力和能力，对你和团队的成功都至关重要。

As a developer you rarely get the time to sit back and really look at how the whole system fits together. As an architect, this is your main focus. While developers are furiously building classes, methods, tests, user interfaces, and databases, you should be making sure that all those pieces work well together. Listen for points of pain and try to improve them. Are people having trouble writing tests? Improve the interfaces and limit dependencies. Do you understand where you actually need abstraction and where you don’t? Work for domain clarity. Do you know what order to build things in? Build your project plan. Are developers consistently making common mistakes using an API you designed? Make the design more obvious. Do people really understand the design? Communicate and make it clear. Do you really understand where you need to scale and where you don’t? Work with your customers and learn their business model.

作为开发，你很少有时间坐下来真正看整个系统怎么拼在一起。作为架构师，这是你的主要关注点。当开发在疯狂写类、方法、测试、用户界面和数据库时，你应该在确保所有这些部分配合良好。倾听痛点并尝试改进。人们写测试有困难？改进接口、限制依赖。你真的理解哪里需要抽象、哪里不需要吗？为领域清晰而努力。你知道该按什么顺序建东西吗？建你的项目计划。开发在用你设计的 API 时一直犯同样的错？让设计更明显。人们真的理解设计吗？沟通并讲清楚。你真的理解哪里需要扩展、哪里不需要吗？和客户一起工作，了解他们的业务模式。

If you’re doing a great job of being an architect, you really shouldn’t have enough time to interfere with developers. You do need to watch closely enough to see that the design is being implemented as intended. You do not need to be standing over people’s shoulders to accomplish that goal. It’s reasonable to make suggestions when you see people struggling, but it’s even better if you create the environment where they come and ask you for suggestions. If you are good, you will deftly walk the fine line between guaranteeing a successful architecture and limiting the creative and intellectual life of your developers and teammates.

如果你架构做得好，你真的不该有时间去干涉开发。你确实需要足够密切地观察设计是否按预期实现。但你不需要站在人背后盯着。看到人挣扎时提建议是合理的，但更好的是你创造一种环境，让他们主动来找你提建议。如果你够好，你会在「保证架构成功」和「限制开发和队友的创造与思想生活」之间走出一条微妙的平衡线。

33. Time Changes Everything

作者：Philip Nelson

One of the things I’ve been most entertained by as the years have gone by is observing what things have lasted and what haven’t. So many patterns, frameworks, paradigm changes, and algorithms—all argued for with passion by smart people, thinking of the long term, balancing all the known issues— have not warranted more than a yawn over the long haul. Why? What is history trying to tell us?

随着年岁增长，我最觉得有意思的事之一是观察什么东西留下来了、什么没有。那么多模式、框架、范式变革和算法——都被聪明人满怀热情地论证过、想着长期、权衡了所有已知问题——长期来看却只值得一个哈欠。为什么？历史想告诉我们什么？

Pick a Worthy Challenge

选一个值得的挑战

This one is tricky for a software architect. Challenges or problems are given to us, so we don’t have the luxury of choosing, right? It’s not that simple. First of all, we often make the mistake of believing that we can’t influence what we are asked to do. Usually we can, but it gets us out of our comfort zone in the technology space. There are dragons there when we don’t choose to do the right things. Time passes, we have worked diligently and hard solving the requested challenge, and in the end it doesn’t matter: we didn’t do what was really needed and our work is wasted. Over time, a good solution to the right challenge will probably outlast all others.

这对软件架构师来说很微妙。挑战或问题是给我们的，所以我们没有选择的奢侈，对吧？没那么简单。首先，我们经常错误地以为自己无法影响被要求做的事。通常我们可以，但那会让我们走出技术上的舒适区。当我们不选择做对的事时，那里有恶龙。时间流逝，我们勤奋努力地解决了被要求的挑战，最后却发现无所谓：我们没做真正需要的事，工作白费了。长期来看，对正确挑战的好方案很可能比所有其他方案都持久。

Simple Rules

简单规则

We say it to ourselves: keep it simple, stupid. We say it, but we don’t do it. We don’t do it because we don’t have to. We are smart and we can handle some

我们对自己说：保持简单，蠢货。我们说了，但没做。我们没做是因为我们不必。我们聪明，能应付一些

complexity and easily justify it because it adds agility to our design, because it is more elegant to our aesthetic sensibilities, because we believe we can anticipate the future. Then time passes; you walk away from the project for a year or more. When you come back to it, you almost always wonder why you did what you did. If you had to do it all over again, you would probably do it differently. Time does this to us. It makes us look silly. It is good to realize this early, get over yourself, and really try to learn what simple means in the lens that only time can grind.

复杂度，并且轻易为它辩护——因为它给设计加了敏捷，因为它对我们的审美更优雅，因为我们相信能预见未来。然后时间流逝；你离开项目一年或更久。再回来时，你几乎总是纳闷自己当时为什么那么做。如果重做一遍，你大概会做得不一样。时间对我们做的就是这个。它让我们看起来傻。早点认识到这一点、别把自己当回事、真正努力去学——只有时间能磨出来的「简单」是什么意思——是好事。

Be Happy with That Old Stuff

对那些老东西满意

Architects love to search for the “one true way”: the methodology or school of thought that provides the predictability we crave and the clear answers that always seem just out of reach. The problem is that whatever guiding light you have in one year will probably not match the guiding light you have in a couple of years, much less a decade later. As you look back, you will always be looking at designs that don’t match your current expectations. Learn to embrace that old stuff, and resist the temptation to think you should go back and “fix” it. Was the solution an appropriate one for the problem? Did it solve the needs of the problem? Keep these as your measure—you will be a lot happier.

架构师喜欢找「唯一真道」：那种能提供我们渴望的可预测性、以及总是差一点够不着的清晰答案的方法论或学派。问题是你一年后信奉的指引之光，大概和几年后、更不用说十年后的不一样。回头看时，你总会看到和你当前期望不匹配的设计。学会拥抱那些老东西，抵制住回去「修」它的诱惑。这个方案对那个问题合适吗？它解决了问题的需要吗？把这些作为你的衡量标准——你会快乐得多。

34. "Software Architect" Has Only Lowercase a's; Deal with It

作者：Barry Hawkins

A disappointing trend  has been in bloom for some time now within software development: the attempt to professionalize the practice of software architecture as one on par with the classical school of Architecture. This seems to stem from some need to further legitimize one’s accomplishment beyond acknowledgment among one’s peers and employer. By comparison, Architecture itself was not professionalized until the late 19th century, at least a few millennia after the practice had been around. It would be no great stretch to say that some software architects seem a bit eager by comparison.

软件开发里有个令人失望的趋势已经开了一阵花：试图把软件架构实践职业化，让它和经典建筑学派平起平坐。这似乎源于某种需要——想让自己的成就超越同事和雇主的认可、进一步合法化。相比之下，建筑学本身直到 19 世纪晚期才职业化，比这门实践存在晚了至少几千年。说有些软件架构师相比之下显得有点急，不算夸张。

Software architecture is a craft, and it certainly takes practice and discipline to achieve success in the field. That said, software development is still a relatively nascent endeavor. We don’t even know enough about this practice to adequately professionalize it. Despite its youth, software development’s product has become a highly valued tool, and as such, the accomplished individuals (as well as those who wish to be seen as accomplished) have enjoyed levels of compensation on par with the leading professional fields, including medicine, accounting, and law.

软件架构是一门手艺，要在这个领域成功确实需要实践和纪律。话虽如此，软件开发仍然是相对新生的事业。我们对这门实践的了解甚至还不够把它充分职业化。尽管年轻，软件开发的产品已经变成高价值工具，因此有成就的人（以及那些想被看作有成就的人）享受到了和医学、会计、法律等领先专业领域相当的报酬。

Practitioners of software development enjoy considerable compensation for work that is highly creative and exploratory. The fruits of our labors have been used to accomplish many significant milestones, some that benefit all of mankind. The barriers to entry are largely one’s own merit and opportunity; the fully professionalized fields undergo programs of study and internship that dwarf our own. Dwell on that for a moment and ponder how much cause we have to be content, and just how brash it is to insist that software architect be considered a title that sits as peer to Lawyer, Doctor, and Architect.

软件开发从业者做的是高度创造性和探索性的工作，却享受相当高的报酬。我们劳动的果实被用来完成了很多重大里程碑，有些造福全人类。进入门槛很大程度上是个人的能力和机会；完全职业化的领域要经过的学习和实习项目让我们的相形见绌。多想一会儿，想想我们有多少理由知足，而坚持说「软件架构师」这个头衔要和律师、医生、建筑师平起平坐，是多么狂妄。

The title of software architect has only lowercase a ’s; deal with it.

软件架构师这个头衔里只有小写的 a；接受它吧。

Barry Hawkins Barry Hawkins has played various roles in his 13 years in the software industry, from lone developer to team lead to Agile coach and mentor. Barry is one of the few native Atlantans, currently specializing in coaching and mentoring for Agile software development and domain-driven design.

Barry Hawkins Barry Hawkins 在软件业 13 年里干过各种角色，从独立开发到团队负责人到敏捷教练和导师。Barry 是少数土生土长的亚特兰大人之一，目前专精敏捷软件开发和领域驱动设计的教练与导师。

35. Scope Is the Enemy of Success

作者：Dave Quick

Scope refers to a project’s size. How much time, effort, and resources? What functionality at what level of quality? How difficult to deliver? How much risk? What constraints exist? The answers define a project’s scope. Software architects love the challenge of big, complicated projects. The potential rewards can even tempt people to artificially expand a project’s scope to increase its apparent importance. Expanding scope is the enemy of success because the probability of failure grows faster than expected. Doubling a project’s scope often increases its probability of failure by an order of magnitude.

范围指项目的大小。多少时间、精力和资源？什么功能、什么质量水平？多难交付？多少风险？有什么约束？这些答案定义项目范围。软件架构师爱大而复杂项目的挑战。潜在回报甚至诱使人为人为扩大项目范围以显得更重要。扩大范围是成功的敌人，因为失败概率比预期增长得更快。把项目范围翻倍，失败概率往往涨一个数量级。

Why does it work this way? Consider some examples:

为什么是这样？看几个例子：

Intuition tells us to double our time or resources to do twice as much • work. History 1 says impacts are not as linear as intuition suggests. For example, a four-person team will expend more than twice the communication effort as a team of two.

直觉告诉我们把时间或资源翻倍做两倍的工作。历史表明影响不像直觉想的那么线性。比如，四人团队的沟通成本是两人团队的两倍多。

Estimation is far from an exact science. Who hasn’t seen features that were • much harder to implement than expected?

估算远不是精确科学。谁没见过比预期难实施得多的功能？

Of course, some projects aren’t worth doing without some built-in size and complexity. While a text editor without the ability to enter text might be easy to build, it wouldn’t be a text editor. So, what strategies can help to reduce or manage scope in real-world projects?

当然，有些项目没有一定的大小和复杂度就不值得做。一个不能输入文字的文本编辑器可能容易建，但它就不是文本编辑器了。那什么策略能帮我们在现实项目中减少或管理范围？

Understand the real needs • . The capabilities a project must deliver are a set of requirements. Requirements define functionality or qualities of functionality. Question any requirements not explained in terms of measurable value to the customer. If it has no effect on the company’s bottom line, why is it a requirement?

理解真实需求。项目必须交付的能力是一组需求。需求定义功能或功能的质量。质疑任何没以可衡量客户价值解释的需求。如果它对公司底线没影响，为什么是需求？

1 See The Mythical Man-Month: Essays on Software Engineering , by Frederick Brooks (Addison-Wesley Professional).

1 参见 Frederick Brooks《人月神话：软件工程随笔》（Addison-Wesley Professional）。

Divide and conquer • . Look for opportunities to divide up the work into smaller independent chunks. It is easier to manage several small independent projects than one large project with interdependent parts.

分而治之。找机会把工作拆成更小的独立块。管理几个小独立项目比管一个各部分相互依赖的大项目容易。

• Prioritize . The world of business changes rapidly. Large projects’ requirements change many times before they’re completed. Important requirements usually remain important as the business changes, while others change or even evaporate. Prioritization lets you deliver the most important requirements first.

排优先级。商业世界变化快。大项目的需求在完成前会变很多次。重要需求通常随业务变化仍重要，其他则变化甚至蒸发。优先级让你先交付最重要的需求。

Deliver results as soon as possible • . Few people know what they want before they have it. A famous cartoon shows the evolution of a project to build a child’s swing based on what the customer said and what various roles in the project understood. The complicated result only faintly resembles a swing. The last panel, titled “What would have worked”, shows a simple swing using an old tire. When the customer has something to try, the solution may be simpler than expected. Building the most important things first gets you the most important feedback early, when you need it most.

尽快交付结果。很少人在拥有之前知道自己想要什么。一幅著名漫画展示了一个儿童秋千项目基于客户说的话和项目中各角色理解的演化过程。复杂结果只是依稀像秋千。最后一 panel 标题是「本来可行的」，展示了一个用旧轮胎做的简单秋千。当客户有东西可试时，方案可能比预期简单。先建最重要的东西让你最早拿到最重要的反馈——在你最需要的时候。

Agile advocates 2 exhort us to build “the simplest thing that could possibly work”. Complex architectures fail far more often than simpler architectures. Reducing project scope often results in a simpler architecture, and is one of the most effective strategies an architect can apply to improve the odds of success.

敏捷倡导者告诫我们建「可能工作的最简单的东西」。复杂架构比简单架构失败多得多。减少项目范围通常带来更简单的架构，是架构师能用来提高成功概率的最有效策略之一。

2 See eXtreme Programming eXplained: Embrace Change , by Kent Beck (Addison-Wesley Professional).

2 参见 Kent Beck《解析极限编程：拥抱变化》（Addison-Wesley Professional）。

36. Value Stewardship Over Showmanship

作者：Barry Hawkins

When an architect enters a project, there is an understandable desire to prove his or her worth. Being assigned the role of software architect typically indicates implicit trust on the part of the company in the architect’s technical leadership, and it only follows that the architect would desire to make good on that expectation as soon as possible. Unfortunately, there are those who labor under the misapprehension that proving one’s worth consists of showmanship—bedazzling if not baffling the team with one’s technical brilliance.

当架构师进入项目时，有一种可以理解的冲动要证明自己的价值。被指派为软件架构师通常意味着公司对架构师技术领导能力的隐含信任，架构师自然想尽快兑现这个期望。不幸的是，有些人误以为证明自己的价值就是表演——用技术 brilliance 把团队 dazzle 甚至 baffling。

Showmanship, the act of appealing to your audience, is important in marketing, but it’s counterproductive to leading a software development project. Architects must win the respect of their team by providing solid leadership and by truly understanding the technical and business domain in which they are expected to operate.

表演——诉诸观众的行为——在营销里重要，但在领导软件开发项目时适得其反。架构师必须通过提供扎实的领导、通过真正理解他们应该在其中运作的技术和业务领域，来赢得团队尊重。

Stewardship, taking responsibility and care of another’s property, is the appropriate role of an architect. An architect must act in the best interests of his customer and not pander to the needs of his own ego.

管家职责—— taking responsibility and care of another's property——才是架构师的合适角色。架构师必须为客户最佳利益行动，而不是迎合自我的需要。

Software architecture is about serving the needs of one’s customers, typically through direction from those with domain expertise that surpasses one’s own. Pursuing successful software development will lead one to create solutions of compromise, balancing the cost and complexity of implementation against the time and effort available to a project. That time and effort are the resources of the company, which the software architect must steward without self-serving undercurrents. Unduly complex systems that sport the latest hot framework or technology buzzword seldom do so without some sacrifice at the company’s expense. Much like an investment broker, the architect is being allowed to play with his client’s money, based on the premise that his activity will yield an acceptable return on investment.

软件架构是关于服务客户需要的，通常是通过那些领域专长超过自己的人的指导。追求成功的软件开发会让你创建妥协方案，在实现成本和复杂度与项目可用时间和精力之间平衡。时间和精力是公司的资源，软件架构师必须不带自利暗流地管家。那些炫着最新热框架或技术热词、过度复杂的系统，很少不牺牲公司利益。就像投资经纪人，架构师被允许用客户的钱玩，前提是他的活动会带来可接受的投资回报。

Value stewardship over showmanship; never forget that you are playing with other people’s money.

重视管家胜过表演；永远别忘了你在玩别人的钱。

37. Software Architecture Has Ethical Consequences

作者：Michael Nygard

The ethical dimension in software is obvious when we are talking about civil rights, identity theft, or malicious software. But it arises in less exotic circumstances. If programs are successful, they affect the lives of thousands or millions of people. That impact can be positive or negative. The program can make their lives better or worse—even if just in minute proportions.

当我们谈公民权利、身份盗窃或恶意软件时，软件的伦理维度很明显。但它出现在不那么 exotic 的场合。如果程序成功，它们影响成千上万甚至数百万人的生活。这种影响可以是正面或负面的。程序可以让他们的生活更好或更坏——即使只是微小比例。

Every time I make a decision about how a program behaves, I am really deciding what my users can and cannot do, in ways more inflexible than law. There is no appeals court for required fields or mandatory workflow.

每次我就程序行为做决定，我实际上是以比法律更不灵活的方式决定用户能做什么、不能做什么。必填字段或强制工作流没有上诉法院。

Another way to think about it is in terms of multipliers. Think back to the last major Internet worm, or when a big geek movie came out. No doubt, you heard or read a story about how much productivity this thing would cost the country. You can always find some analyst with an estimate of outrageous damages, blamed on anything that takes people away from their desks. The real moral of this story isn’t about innumeracy in the press, or self-aggrandizing accountants. It’s about multipliers, and the effect they can have.

另一个思考方式是用乘数。回想上一次重大互联网蠕虫，或一部大热极客电影上映。毫无疑问，你听到或读到过这个东西会让国家损失多少生产力。你总能找到某个分析师给出离谱损失估计，怪罪于任何让人离开办公桌的东西。这个故事真正的寓意不是新闻界的不识数，或会计师的自吹自擂。它是关于乘数以及乘数能有的效应。

Suppose you have a decision to make about a particular feature. You can do it the easy way in about a day, or the hard way in about a week. Which way should you do it? Suppose that the easy way makes four new fields required, whereas doing it the hard way makes the program smart enough to handle incomplete data. Which way should you do it?

假设你要就一个特定功能做决定。你可以用简单办法做，大约一天；或者用难办法，大约一周。该用哪个？假设简单办法让四个新字段成为必填，而难办法让程序足够聪明能处理不完整数据。该用哪个？

Required fields seem innocuous, but they are always an imposition of your will on users. They force users to gather more information before starting their jobs. This often means they have to keep their data on Post-It notes until they’ve got everything together at the same time, resulting in lost data, delays, and general frustration.

必填字段看起来无害，但它们总是把你的意志强加给用户。它们迫使用户在开始工作前收集更多信息。这经常意味着他们得把数据写在便利贴上，直到同时凑齐所有东西，结果是数据丢失、延迟和普遍挫败。

As an analogy, suppose I’m putting up a sign on my building. Is it OK to mount the sign just six feet up on the wall, forcing pedestrians to duck or go around it? It’s easier for me to hang the sign if I don’t need a ladder and scaffold, and the sign wouldn’t even block the sidewalk. I get to save an hour installing the sign, at the expense of taking two seconds away from every pedestrian passing my store. Over the long run, all of those two-second diversions are going to add up to many, many times more than the hour that I saved.

打个比方，假设我在自己楼上挂个招牌。把招牌只挂在墙上 6 英尺高、迫使行人低头或绕路，行吗？我挂招牌时不需要梯子和脚手架会更容易，而且招牌甚至不挡人行道。我省了一小时装招牌，代价是从每个路过我店的行人那里拿走两秒。长期来看，所有那些两秒的分心加起来，会比我省的那一小时多很多倍。

It’s not ethical to worsen the lives of others, even a small bit, just to make things easy for yourself. Successful software affects millions of people. Every decision you make imposes your will on your users. Always be mindful of the impact your decisions have on those people. You should be willing to bear large burdens to ease theirs.

哪怕只是一点点让别人生活变差，只为了让自己方便，都是不道德的。成功的软件影响数百万人。你做的每个决定都把你的意志强加给用户。永远注意你的决定对这些人的影响。你应该愿意承担重担来减轻他们的重担。

38. Skyscrapers Aren't Scalable

作者：Michael Nygard

We often hear software engineering compared to building skyscrapers, dams, or roads. It’s true in some important aspects.

我们经常听到软件工程被比作建摩天大楼、水坝或道路。在一些重要方面确实如此。

The hardest part of civil engineering isn’t designing a building that will stand up once it is finished, but figuring out the construction process. The construction process has to go from a bare site to a finished building. In the interim, every worker must be able to apply his trade, and the unfinished structure has to stand up the whole time. We can take a lesson from that when it comes to deploying large integrated systems. (“Integrated” includes virtually every enterprise and web application!) Traditional “big bang” deployments are like stacking up a pile of beams and girders, throwing them into the air, and expecting them to stick together in the shape of a building.

土木工程最难的部分不是设计一栋完工后能立住的楼，而是搞清楚施工过程。施工过程必须从一片空地到一栋完工大楼。其间每个工人都能干活，未完成的结构一直得立着。部署大型集成系统时我们可以从中学到一课。（「集成」几乎包括所有企业和 Web 应用！）传统「大爆炸」部署就像把一堆梁柱堆起来、扔到空中、期望它们粘成大楼形状。

Instead, we should plan to deploy one component at a time. Whether this is a replacement or a greenfield project, this has two large benefits.

相反，我们应该计划一次部署一个组件。不管这是替换还是全新项目，这有两个大好处。

First, when we deploy software, we are exposing ourselves to the accumulated technical risk embodied in the code. By deploying one component at a time, we spread technical risk out over a longer period of time. Every component has its own chance to fail in production, letting us harden each one independently.

第一，部署软件时，我们是在把自己暴露给代码中累积的技术风险。一次部署一个组件，我们把技术风险摊到更长时间里。每个组件都有机会在生产中失败，让我们独立加固每个。

The second large benefit is that it forces us to create well-defined interfaces between components. Deploying a single component of a new system often means reverse-integrating it with the old system. Therefore, by the time deployment is complete, each component has worked with two different systems: the original and the replacement. Nothing is reusable until it has been reused, so piecewise deployment automatically means greater reusability. In practice, it also leads to better coherence and looser coupling.

第二个大好处是它迫使我们在组件之间创建定义良好的接口。部署新系统的单个组件通常意味着要把它和旧系统反向集成。因此到部署完成时，每个组件已经和两个不同系统工作过：原始的和替换的。东西没被复用之前都不算可复用，所以分段部署自动意味着更好的可复用性。实践中它还带来更好的内聚和更松的耦合。

Conversely, there are some important ways that civil engineering analogies mislead us. In particular, the concreteness of the real world pushes us toward a waterfall process. After all, nobody starts building a skyscraper without knowing where it’s going or how tall it should be. Adding floors to an existing building is costly, disruptive, and risky, so we try to avoid it. Once designed, the skyscraper isn’t supposed to change its location or height. Skyscrapers aren’t scalable.

反过来，土木工程类比在一些重要方面会误导我们。特别是，现实世界的具体性把我们推向瀑布过程。毕竟没人会在不知道摩天楼要在哪、多高的情况下开始建。在现有楼上加楼层代价高、 disruptive、有风险，所以我们尽量避免。一旦设计好，摩天楼不应该改变位置或高度。摩天大楼不可扩展。

We cannot easily add lanes to roads, but we’ve learned how to easily add features to software. This isn’t a defect of our software processes, but a virtue of the medium in which we work. It’s OK to release an application that only does a few things, as long as users value those things enough to pay for them. In fact, the earlier you release your application, the greater the net present value of the whole thing will be.

我们不能轻易给道路加车道，但我们学会了轻易给软件加功能。这不是软件过程的缺陷，而是我们工作介质的优点。发布一个只做几件事的应用是可以的，只要用户足够看重那些事愿意付钱。事实上，越早发布应用，整个东西的净现值越高。

“Early release” may appear to compete with “incremental deployment,” but they can actually work together quite well. Early release of individual components means that each one can iterate independently. In fact, it will force you to work out thorny issues like continuous availability during deployments and protocol versioning.

「早发布」看起来和「增量部署」冲突，但它们其实可以很好地协同工作。单个组件早发布意味着每个都能独立迭代。事实上，它会迫使你解决棘手问题，比如部署期间的持续可用性和协议版本管理。

It’s rare to find a technique that simultaneously provides higher commercial value and better architectural qualities, but early deployment of individual components offers both.

很少有技术能同时提供更高商业价值和更好架构质量，但单个组件的早部署两者都提供。

39. Heterogeneity Wins

作者：Edward Garson

The natural evolution of computer technology has brought about important changes to the tools that architects can use to build software systems. These changes have brought about a resurgence of interest in polyglot programming, which refers to the use of more than one core language in the provision of a software system.

计算机技术的自然演化给架构师用来构建软件系统的工具带来了重要变化。这些变化重新点燃了对多语言编程的兴趣——指在提供软件系统时使用不止一种核心语言。

Polyglot programming is not a new concept: one prominent example from the past is frontend Visual Basic clients supported by COM objects authored in C++ on the backend. Fundamentally speaking, this architecture leveraged what those languages were good at in their heyday.

多语言编程不是新概念：过去一个突出例子是前端 Visual Basic 客户端，由后端 C++ 写的 COM 对象支持。从根本上说，这个架构利用了那些语言在鼎盛时期擅长的东西。

So, what changes took place to fuel this renewed interest in polyglot ­programming?

那是什么变化点燃了对多语言编程的新兴趣？

The change is that technical standards, together with ever-increasing bandwidth and computing resources, conspired to make text-based protocols viable; gone are the days of arcane binary protocols as a prerequisite to efficient distributed systems. Text-based remote interoperability largely began with XML/SOAPbased web services and continues to evolve with RESTful architectural styles and other supporting (but no less important) protocols such as Atom and XMPP.

变化是：技术标准加上不断增长的带宽和计算资源，合谋让基于文本的协议可行；那种把晦涩二进制协议作为高效分布式系统前提的日子一去不复返了。基于文本的远程互操作很大程度上始于 XML/SOAP Web 服务，并随着 RESTful 架构风格和其他支持（但同样重要）协议如 Atom 和 XMPP 继续演化。

This new breed of technologies creates far broader opportunities for heterogeneous development than ever before, simply because the payload is formatted text, which is universally generated and consumed. Heterogeneous development affords using the right tool for the job, and text-based interop has blown the doors off what was previously possible.

这种新技术品种为异构开发创造了比以往广泛得多的机会，原因很简单：payload 是格式化文本，被普遍生成和消费。异构开发允许用合适的工具做合适的事，而基于文本的互操作为以前可能的东西打开了大门。

Architects can now combine specific, powerful tools that move the yardstick from previously being able to employ the right language to now being able to employ the right paradigm. Programming languages support different paradigms, in that some are object-oriented, while others are functional or excel

架构师现在可以组合特定的、强大的工具，把标尺从以前能雇用合适语言，推到现在能雇用合适范式。编程语言支持不同范式——有些面向对象，另一些函数式，或在并发编程上出色。

at concurrent programming. Some of these paradigms are a perfect match for particular problems or domains, while others are a poor fit. Today, however, it is possible to “mash up” some rather unconventional and seemingly dissonant tools into elegant solutions rather more easily than in the past.

这些范式中有些和特定问题或领域完美匹配，另一些则不匹配。然而今天，把相当非常规、看似不和谐的工具「混搭」成优雅方案，比以前容易多了。

The effect of this change has begun, and manifests itself as a combinatorial increase in the architectural topology of modern software systems. This is not just a reflection of their inherent diversity, but a testament to new possibilities.

这个变化的效应已经开始，表现为现代软件系统架构拓扑的组合式增长。这不仅反映了它们内在的多样性，更是新可能性的证明。

While choice is not always a good thing, it is “less worse” than the alternative in the context of modern software architecture. As an industry, we are faced with very serious problems 1 and we need all the interoperability we can get, particularly as the incumbent platforms are not well equipped to resolve them. 2

虽然选择不总是好事，但在现代软件架构语境下它比替代方案「没那么糟」。作为一个行业，我们面临非常严重的问题，我们需要所有能得到的互操作性——特别是现有平台没准备好解决它们。

Your job as architect has become even more challenging because technology silos are crumbling in the face of new possibilities: embrace this, think outside the stack, and leverage the new diversity: heterogeneity wins.

你作为架构师的工作变得更有挑战，因为技术竖井在新可能性面前正在崩塌：拥抱这一点，跳出技术栈思维，利用新的多样性：异构取胜。

Edward Garson Edward Garson has been passionate about technology since learning to program in Logo on the Apple II. He currently works as a software architect in the Center for Agile Practices at Zuhlke Engineering, a leading Swiss-based technology firm. 1 The impending multicore era may well prove to be the most significant problem yet faced by the software development community. 2 See “The Free Lunch is Over,” by Herb Sutter ( http://www.gotw.ca/publications/concurrency-ddj.htm ) .

Edward Garson Edward Garson 从在 Apple II 上用 Logo 学编程起就热爱技术。他目前是 Zuhlke Engineering（一家领先的瑞士技术公司）敏捷实践中心的软件架构师。

40. It's All About Performance

作者：Craig Russell

Imagine a personal vehicle that is roomy, comfortable, fuel efficient, inexpensive to produce, and 98% recyclable. You want one? Sure. Everyone does. Just one problem: its top speed is 6 miles/hour (10 km/hour). Still want one? This small example demonstrates that performance is just as important as any other criterion.

想象一辆个人用车：宽敞、舒适、省油、生产成本低、98% 可回收。你想要一辆？当然，谁都想。只有一个问题：最高时速 6 英里（约 10 公里）。还想要吗？这个小例子说明性能和任何其他标准一样重要。

The reason many designers put performance at the bottom of their lists might be that computers are so much faster at computation than their human counterparts that the designers assume that the speed of the system will be acceptable. And if today’s systems aren’t fast enough, Moore’s Law will take care of everything. But hardware speed is only part of the system.

很多设计师把性能放清单底部，可能是因为计算机计算比人快太多，设计师就假设系统速度可接受。如果今天的系统不够快，摩尔定律会解决一切。但硬件速度只是系统的一部分。

Performance is sometimes thought of as a simple measurement of the time it takes for a system to respond to user input. But system designers must consider many aspects of performance, including performance of the analysts and programmers who implement the design; performance of the human interactions of the system; and performance of the noninteractive components.

性能有时被简单认为是系统响应用户输入所花时间的度量。但系统设计师必须考虑性能的很多方面：实现设计的分析师和程序员的性能；系统人际交互的性能；以及非交互组件的性能。

Performance of the people building the system is often called productivity, and it is important because it directly affects the cost and schedule of the project. A team that delivers a project late and over budget has a lot of ‘splainin’ to do. Using tools and prebuilt components can dramatically affect how quickly the system can be built and start returning value.

建系统的人的性能通常叫生产力，它重要因为直接影响项目成本和进度。一个晚交付、超预算的团队有很多要解释的。用工具和预构建组件能极大影响系统多快能建好并开始回报价值。

Performance of the human interactions is critical to acceptance of the system. Many factors of system design contribute to this aspect of performance, response time being perhaps the most obvious. But response time isn’t the only

人际交互的性能对系统接受度至关重要。系统设计的很多因素贡献这方面性能，响应时间也许最明显。但响应时间不是唯一

factor. Just as important are intuitiveness of the interface and number of gestures required to achieve a goal, both of which directly affect performance.

因素。同样重要的是界面的直观性和达成一个目标所需的手势数量，两者都直接影响性能。

More than response time per se, a good system specification will measure task time, defined as the time required to complete a domain-specific task, including all human interactions with the system. In addition to system response time, this measurement includes operator think time and operator data entry time, which are not under the control of the system. But including these times gives motivation to the proper design of the human interface. Proper attention to the way information is presented and the number of gestures required to complete the task will result in better human operational performance.

好的系统规格衡量的不只是响应时间本身，而是任务时间——完成一个领域特定任务所需的时间，包括所有人机交互。除了系统响应时间，这个度量还包括操作员思考时间和数据录入时间——这些不在系统控制下。但把这些时间算进去，会促使人机界面的正确设计。适当关注信息呈现方式和完成任务所需手势数量，会带来更好的人的操作性能。

Performance of the noninteractive components is equally important to the success of the system. For example, a “nightly” batch run that takes more than 24 hours to complete will result in an unusable system. Performance of the disaster recovery component is also a critical consideration. In case of total destruction of one part of the system, how quickly can operational status be restored, in order to allow normal business to resume?

非交互组件的性能对系统成功同样重要。比如，一个要跑超过 24 小时的「夜间」批处理会导致系统不可用。灾难恢复组件的性能也是关键考虑。如果系统一部分完全被毁，多快能恢复运行状态、让正常业务恢复？

When considering the implementation and operation of a successful system, architects and designers should always pay careful attention to performance.

考虑成功系统的实现和运营时，架构师和设计师应该始终仔细关注性能。

Craig Russell Craig Russell is a practicing software architect specializing in object persistence and distributed systems. He currently works as a senior staff engineer at Sun Microsystems.

Craig Russell Craig Russell 是执业软件架构师，专责对象持久化和分布式系统。他目前是 Sun Microsystems 的高级工程师。
